🌀 Complex Hyperbolic Functions

On the real line ||(\sinh||) and ||(\cosh||) are boring: they just grow. Step off the real axis and they turn out to be periodic wallpaper — the same functions as ||(\sin||) and ||(\cos||), merely rotated a quarter turn in the complex plane: ||[\sinh(iz) = i\,\sin z \qquad\qquad \cosh(iz) = \cos z||]Everything below is live — drag things.

The pattern repeats forever up and down — that is what real-line plots hide.</span></span></div>

data.text/markdown:
Properties of ||(\sinh z = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(e^{z} - e^{-z}\right)||)
period ||(2\pi i||) — invisible on the real line
parity odd
zeros ||(z = n\pi i||)
poles none — entire (analytic everywhere)
real/imag split ||(\sinh(x+iy) = \sinh x\,\cos y + i\,\cosh x\,\sin y||)
trig twin ||(\sinh(iz) = i\sin z||)
reflection ||(f(\bar z) = \overline{f(z)}||) — real on the real axis
All zeros and poles are simple and sit on the imaginary axis, spaced ||(\pi||) apart. Since these functions are periodic and meromorphic, the entire complex plane is just one vertical strip of height ||(2\pi i||) stamped over and over.
The punchline: hyperbolic is trigonometric, rotated
